newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover shoots up after holidays.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover shoots up after holidays.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) reported on Monday a 658.25 percent increase during the week ending May 9, but dramatic changes resulted from the BSE getting back to its normal activity after a week of holidays.
The bourse worked only two days in the week ending May 2, due to a long Orthodox Easter weekend and a two-day May 1 Labour day Holiday.
Total BSE turnover rose to 32.999 million dinars in 219 transactions, from 4.352 million dinars in 25 deals a week ago.
Traders said overall liquidity of the market remained poor leading companies to focus their activity on the commercial paper segment.
"Companies continued to seek fresh funds via commercial paper, but in most cases it is still revolving of old borrowing," a trader told Reuters.
For the week ending May 9, the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper traded 212 times for a volume of 31.074 million dinars.
* Treasury bills traded twice for a total of 0.2 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between a monthly 9.50 and 16.42 percent, while maturity stood between two and 30 days.
* The central bank sold a further 1.225 million dinars worth of bonds from its portfolio. Bonds, issued by the Serbian Commodity Reserve Agency, were sold on the secondary market.
* There were two transactions in certificates of deposit, worth 0.5 million dinars.
* Over-the-counter trade in commercial paper and treasury bills stood at 26.615 million dinars. The BSE gave no comparative figures for the previous week.

* OTC trade in giro money, with banks trading their surplus liquidity, stood at 31.8 million dinars, but no comparative figures for the previous week were available. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
